correctness.rationale: For each elementary face, one surviving vertex covers it completely; when none survives, only three opposite lattice sites can cover any of its interior, by projection to its edges. Their unit disks yield disjoint caps of area pi/6-sqrt3/4 and arc length pi/3, giving exact deterministic area/perimeter by counting boundary sides. Independence gives q^3 and q^3(1-q) weights; ergodic theorem gives area/length densities. Numerical checks corroborate independently but no finite test proves infinitely many patterns.

value.rationale: An exact deterministic continuum-to-combinatorial valuation computes uncovered area and boundary length from a finite-site erasure pattern of arbitrary shape and size, and yields explicit spatial damage fraction and interface-density laws at every independent failure probability. Face adjacency produces a strictly positive quantitative interaction and the first coverage failure has a sharp three-site threshold, making the invariant useful for exact geometrical reliability calculations, beyond a stand-alone exercise in segment area.
